title: GENEROUS ENOUGH TO SHARE THE SPIRIT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: However, two men, whose names were Eldad and Medad, had remained in the camp. They were listed among the elders, but did not go out to the tent. Yet the Spirit also rested on them, and they prophesied in the camp. A young man ran and told Moses, "Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp." Joshua son of Nun, who had been Moses' aide since youth, spoke up and said, "Moses, my lord, stop them!" But Moses replied, "Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all the Lord's people were prophets and that the Lord would put his Spirit on them!" — Num 11:26-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two of the seventy, Eldad and Medad, never made it to the tent — yet the Spirit rested on them right there in the camp. God's Spirit is not bound by our locations or our tidy expectations. He blesses whom He will, where He will.

Young Joshua, zealous and protective of Moses, wanted them stopped. It looked like a threat to Moses' unique authority. But Moses' response is stunningly generous: "Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all the Lord's people were prophets!" Far from guarding his own position, Moses longed for everyone to know the Spirit's power.

This exposes a temptation that quietly grips many of us: we can become territorial about God's work. We feel threatened when others are gifted, blessed, or used by God, as if His favour on them somehow diminishes us. Joshua's instinct was to protect the leader; Moses' heart was to see God's kingdom spread.

Moses' longing was answered centuries later. At Pentecost, God poured out His Spirit on all His people, exactly as Moses wished. If you follow Christ, you carry the Spirit Moses hoped everyone would have. Let that make you generous, not territorial — celebrating rather than resenting how God works in others.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you ever feel threatened when God blesses or uses others?
2. What would it look like to celebrate others' gifts instead of guarding your own place?
3. How does the gift of the Spirit to all believers shape your attitude?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, free me from jealousy and territorial pride. Give me Moses' generous heart that longs to see Your Spirit at work in everyone. Let me celebrate Your grace wherever it appears. Amen.
